newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on wet weather outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on wet weather outlook.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended lower on Monday after forecasts for wetter weather this weekend overrode concerns that persistent dry weather had cut yield potential, traders said.

Forecasts called for a cool, dry week for the U.S. Midwest but Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said Monday that computer guidance models suggested a shift to a wetter pattern this weekend and next week.
"This morning's (Monday) computer guidance indicates that by this weekend and next week (the week of August 11) there will some changes in the pattern," Davis wrote.
"Plain and simply, this pattern is much more favorable for widespread rains in the central U.S.," he added.
Corn had rallied sharply last week and in Project A overnight trade Sunday on concerns persistent dry weather would stress the corn crop.

The trade is expecting the U.S. Agriculture Department's weekly crop update will show a deterioration in the U.S. corn crop following last week's dry weather. The update was slated for release Monday at 1500 CDT.
Corn ended four to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower with December down four at $2.65.
The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook, released after the close of trading Monday, also suggested a wetter pattern for Illinois with below normal temperatures.

World weather patterns drew bearish reviews. Rains fell in northern China over the weekend bringing some relief to drought-stricken areas but traders said the moisture came too late to rescue the corn crop which suffered from heat and moisture stress during July, the key pollination month.
"Corn has been hurt already and the rains won't do us all that much good," Dean Witter's Gidel said.

The export front offered little support despite news Taiwan was likely to tender for 108,000 tonnes. The USDA weekly export sales data came in at 20,833,000 bushels, below expectations for 24 million to 28 million.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report held few surprises for the market.

"We're getting them (funds) long corn and we're running the shorts out of beans," a trader said referring to the market activity Wednesday through Thursday. The CFTC data was based on market positions as of Tuesday, July 29.

CFTC said non-commercials as of Tuesday were long corn by 147.815 million bushels and short by 152.658 million. Commercials were long corn by about 667.560 million bushels and short by 494.030 million.
Technically, traders said the market closed above support at $2.63 per bushel in the December. That level marked the 50 percent retracement point from the year's highs, Gidel said.

On the day, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer sold at least 15 million bushels December while Cargill Investor Services sold 11 million December. Refco Inc and Griffin Trading were on both sides of the market and Term Commodities bought one million September, traders said.
Continental Grain bear spread five million December/September at 1-1/2 cents, premium December, and Tenco Inc spread two million December/September at 1-1/2.
In options, Griffin bought 1,000 December $2.60 puts at 12 cents and 1,000 December $2.50 puts at 7-1/2 to 8-1/2 cents. Griffin also sold 750 December $3.00 calls at five cents.
CIS sold 1,000 December $2.60 calls at 16-1/2 cents.
Volatility in the September closed at 32 percent, against Friday's 32-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 90,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 75,272. Options volume was pegged at 26,000 contracts, against Friday's 32,094.
